question: Who among the following has authored the play 'Nil Darpan'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinabandhu Mitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dinabandhu Mitra was a notable Bengali dramatist of the 19th century.
 
• He wrote the play 'Nil Darpan' in 1860-61, which portrays the plight of indigo farmers under British rule in Bengal.
 
• 'Nil Darpan' is considered a significant work in Bengali literature and played a crucial role in the Indigo revolt of 1859-60.
 
• The play was translated into English by Reverend James Long, which led to his imprisonment and fine due to its anti-British sentiments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigo Rebellion:**

 
 
• The Indigo Rebellion (or Indigo Revolt) was a peasant movement and subsequent uprising against indigo planters in Bengal in 1859-60.
 
• Indigo farmers were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions and received meager payment.
 
• The rebellion highlighted the exploitation by British planters and led to reforms in the indigo cultivation practices.
 
 
 
• **Bengali Literature:**
 
 
• Bengali literature is one of the richest literary traditions in the Indian subcontinent, with works dating back to the 10th century.
 
• It encompasses a wide range of genres, including poetry, drama, novels, short stories, and essays.
 
• Notable figures in Bengali literature include Rabindranath Tagore, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, and Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Rule in India:**
 
 
• British colonial rule in India lasted from 1858 to 1947, following the transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown after the Revolt of 1857.
 
• During this period, India was subjected to economic exploitation, cultural changes, and political reorganization.
 
• Significant events during British rule include the establishment of the Indian National Congress, the Partition of Bengal, and the struggle for Indian independence led by figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
